Except where otherwise indicated, all financial information reflected herein is expressed in Canadian dollars. The following section generally discusses 2025 and 2024 items and includes comparisons between 2025 and 2024. Discussions of 2023 items and comparisons between 2024 and 2023 that are not included in this Form 10-K can be found in Item 7. Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations of the Company's Annual Report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2024. For purposes of this report, unless the context indicates otherwise, all references herein to "CPKC", "the Company" or "our" refer to Canadian Pacific Kansas City Limited ("CPKC") and its subsidiaries. Executive Summary 2025 Results • Total revenues were $15,078 million, an increase of 4% compared to $14,546 million in 2024. The increase was primarily due to higher volumes as measured by revenue ton-miles ("RTMs"). • Diluted earnings per share ("EPS") was $4.51, an increase of 13% compared to $3.98 in 2024. • Core adjusted diluted EPS was $4.61, an increase of 8% compared to $4.25 in 2024. • Operating ratio was 62.8%, a 160 basis point improvement from 64.4% in 2024. • Core adjusted operating ratio was 59.9%, a 140 basis point improvement from 61.3% in 2024. Core adjusted diluted EPS and Core adjusted operating ratio are defined and reconciled in the "Non-GAAP Measures" section of this Item 7. passages.heading: Risk factors
passages.text: The risks set forth in the following risk factors could have a materially adverse effect on the Company's business, financial condition, results of operations, and liquidity, and could cause those results to differ materially from those expressed or implied in the Company's forward-looking statements and forward-looking information (collectively, "forward-looking statements"). The information set forth in this Item 1A. Risk Factors should be read in conjunction with the rest of the information included in this Annual Report on Form 10-K, including Part II Item 7. Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations and Item 8. Financial Statements and Supplementary Data. Business and Operational Risks As a common carrier, the Company is required by law to transport dangerous goods and hazardous materials, which could expose the Company to significant costs and claims. Railways, including the Company, are legally required to transport dangerous goods and hazardous materials as part of their common carrier obligations regardless of risk or potential exposure to loss. The Company transports dangerous goods and hazardous materials, including but not limited to crude oil, ethanol, and TIH materials such as chlorine gas and anhydrous ammonia. A train accident involving hazardous materials could result in significant claims against the Company arising from personal injury, property or natural resource damage, environmental penalties, and remediation obligations. Such claims, if insured, could exceed the existing insurance coverage commercially available to the Company, which could have a material adverse effect on the Company’s financial condition, operating results, and liquidity. The Company is also required to comply with rules and regulations regarding the handling of dangerous goods and hazardous materials across its network. Noncompliance with these rules and regulations can subject the Company to significant penalties and could factor in litigation arising out of a train accident. Changes to these rules and regulations could also increase operating costs, reduce operating efficiencies and impact service delivery. The Company faces competition from other transportation providers and failure to compete effectively could adversely affect financial results. The Company faces significant competition for freight transportation across its network, including competition from other railways, motor carriers, ship and barge operators, and pipelines. Competition is based mainly on quality of service, freight rates, and access to markets. Other transportation modes generally use public rights-of-way that are built and maintained by government entities, while the Company and other railways must use internal resources to build and maintain their rail networks. Competition with the trucking industry is generally based on freight rates, flexibility of service, and transit time performance. credit_strengths.text: CPKC's operating margin is exceptionally high relative to the Industrials sector median, reflecting the efficiency of its rail network and pricing power. This strong profitability, combined with stable revenue growth, provides a substantial buffer to absorb volume or cost shocks and supports consistent cash generation through the cycle.

Operating cash flow covers interest expense multiple times over, and free cash flow after capital expenditure remains positive. This internally generated liquidity is a core credit strength, reducing reliance on external funding for routine capital needs and providing capacity to service debt even under moderate earnings pressure.

key_risks.text: CPKC is legally required to transport dangerous goods, including crude oil, ethanol, and toxic inhalation hazards such as chlorine gas and anhydrous ammonia. A train accident involving these materials could generate claims exceeding available insurance coverage, with material adverse effects on financial condition, operating results, and liquidity.

The debt maturity profile concentrates a significant portion of borrowings in the next twelve months, alongside a large commercial paper balance. Refinancing this near-term maturities wall depends on continued access to debt capital markets, and any disruption could strain liquidity given the modest cash balance relative to current liabilities.

debt_servicing_capacity.text: Interest coverage is solid but sits below the sector median, indicating less headroom than peers. With leverage above the sector median and an indicative financial risk profile of Significant, debt servicing capacity is adequate but sensitive to EBITDA declines; a moderate earnings drop could pressure the current tier.

Free cash flow to debt is modest and well below the sector median, while cash flow to debt also lags peers. Shareholder distributions, including dividends and buybacks, absorb a substantial share of operating cash flow, limiting the pace of deleveraging and leaving less cushion for debt reduction.

overall_credit_view.text: CPKC's credit profile balances strong operating profitability and consistent cash generation against leverage that is above the sector median and a concentrated near-term maturity profile. The indicative financial risk profile is Significant, with limited headroom to the next leverage threshold, suggesting a stable but not strong credit standing.

Our forward-looking view is that debt servicing capacity will remain adequate, supported by predictable rail cash flows, but shareholder returns and capital spending will likely keep free cash flow after distributions thin. A material operating setback or refinancing difficulty could weaken metrics, and we would monitor leverage and liquidity closely.

credit_strengths.text: CPKC的營運利潤率相對於工業板塊中位數異常偏高，反映其鐵路網絡的效率及定價能力。此強勁的盈利能力，加上穩定的收入增長，提供了厚實的緩衝以吸收運量或成本衝擊，並支持整個週期內持續的現金產生。
營運現金流覆蓋利息支出達數倍，且扣除資本開支後自由現金流仍為正數。此內部產生的流動性為核心信用優勢，減少對外部資金應付日常資本需求的依賴，並提供能力在盈利溫和受壓下仍可償付債務。

key_risks.text: CPKC依法須運輸危險品，包括原油、乙醇及有毒吸入危害物如氯氣及無水氨。涉及此等材料的列車事故可能產生超出可用保險覆蓋的索賠，對財務狀況、經營業績及流動性造成重大不利影響。
債務到期結構將顯著部分借款集中於未來十二個月，同時有龐大商業票據餘額。為此近期到期牆再融資取決於能否持續進入債務資本市場，任何干擾可能令流動性受壓，因現金餘額相對於流動負債而言適度。

debt_servicing_capacity.text: 利息覆蓋率穩健但低於板塊中位數，顯示較同業為少的緩衝。槓桿高於板塊中位數且指示性財務風險狀況為Significant，債務償付能力足夠但對EBITDA下降敏感；盈利溫和下跌可能令當前級別受壓。
自由現金流對債務比率適度且遠低於板塊中位數，而現金流對債務亦落後同業。股東分派包括股息及回購，佔營運現金流相當份額，限制去槓桿步伐並減少債務削減的緩衝。

overall_credit_view.text: CPKC的信用狀況平衡強勁營運盈利能力及持續現金產生，對比高於板塊中位數的槓桿及集中的近期到期結構。指示性財務風險狀況為Significant，距下一槓桿門檻的緩衝有限，顯示信用狀況穩定但不強勁。
我們的前瞻觀點是債務償付能力將保持足夠，受可預測的鐵路現金流支持，但股東回報及資本開支可能令扣除分派後自由現金流保持稀薄。重大營運挫折或再融資困難可能削弱指標，我們將密切監察槓桿及流動性。
